I wasn't expecting that at all.
What were you doing when it happened?
Two hundred people were sitting still.
An actor was walking towards the front of the stage.
At quarter past eight the lights went out.
He was standing in the same place when the lights came on.
The lights went out while the actor was walking to the front of the stage.
I wasn't expecting that, and neither was anybody else.
For a moment nobody realized what was happening.
Meanwhile, everybody outside was waiting for the bus in the dark.
And you? What were you doing when it happened?

Everybody in my family remembers where they were, and none of us remembers the same thing. My mother says she was cooking. My brother says she was on the phone and the pan was burning. I was nine. I was lying on the floor doing homework I was not really doing, and the television was on with the sound down. Then the phone rang and my mother went very quiet, and my brother and I looked at each other, because children always know before anybody tells them. What I remember is not the news itself. I remember that the fan was turning, that somebody outside was cutting the grass, and that my pencil rolled under the sofa and I never got it back. Thirty years later I could draw that room for you. I could not tell you a single word anybody said.

There is a good reason why you remember the background of a bad moment better than the moment itself. While something ordinary is going on, your brain is barely writing anything down. It is running on the idea that today is the same as yesterday, so there is nothing to save. Then something breaks the pattern, and for about ninety seconds it writes down everything, including the parts that do not matter at all. The smell. The shoes. What was playing. So the fan, the grass outside, the pencil under the sofa are not sentimental details. They are the last frame of the ordinary, kept because it was still on the desk when the alarm went off. It is also why people say the strangest sentence in the language. I remember exactly what I was doing. Not what happened. What they were doing.
